note: Adapted from Light & Wilson 1936, original in English (The nasute termites of the Philippines, The Philippine Journal of Science 60: 461–520). Both the alate and the worker are given as Unknown in the original; a single lot, collected by Taylor on Jolo Island, type collection No. 314. Fig. 17 (soldier head in dorsal and lateral view, left mandible) not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Very small, body length under 3 mm; head shape peculiar — nasus peak projecting, front of the head concave, base of the nasus markedly narrowed, with a distinct anteriorly pointed projection on each side at the base of the nasus; free part of the mandible reduced; antennae 11-segmented. These characters distinguish it from the other Philippine species and from the other species of the genus known to the authors.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head greyish smoky yellowish brown; nasus pale brown; abdominal tergites very faintly pigmented. Very small, body length under 3 mm. Head and nasus shape as in Fig. 17 a, b: nasus peak projecting; front of the head concave; nasus narrowed near the base, with a distinct anteriorly pointed projection on each side at its base. Head covered with a layer of long fine curved white hairs and very few stiff bristle-like hairs. Free part of the mandible reduced. Antennae 11-segmented. Measurements (mm and indices, from type collection No. 314, a typical soldier from Jolo Island): head plus nasus 1.20; head length (excluding nasus) 0.76; nasus length 0.44; head projection 0.27; head height 0.48; head width 0.69; fore tibia length 0.54; head index 0.91; head-nasus index 0.57; head projection index 0.35; leg extension index 0.71.
